Yes, if no build with `is.waiwai.dictation` has reached anyone but you and your testers. Pre-launch is the cheapest time to do it.

**What the rule protects:** macOS ties Accessibility permission to the bundle ID. After a rename, the app counts as a new app and everyone has to re-grant access. Sparkle may also refuse to update an old-ID install to a new-ID build. I haven't checked that against your Sparkle version, so I wouldn't count on it working. Preferences, keychain items, and Application Support paths keyed to the old ID would move too.

**If real users already have an old-ID build:** don't rename. The permission loss and a possibly broken update path cost more than the naming benefit.

**If it's only dev and test builds:** rename. The cost is one re-grant on your own machines, plus these steps:
- Change the ID everywhere (Info.plist, entitlements, build and release scripts, `docs/release.md`, `AGENTS.md`).
- Reset the old grant with `tccutil reset Accessibility is.waiwai.dictation`.
- Keep the same Sparkle EdDSA key.
- Keep signing nested code inside-out, with no `--deep`.
- Update the "permanent" invariant to say the new ID is permanent from launch.

Has any build with the old ID been shipped outside your own machines? If not, tell me to go and I'll make the change.
